content: 1. Both midine and pentamidine can increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. 2. Crizotinib and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. ECG monitoring is recommended, especially when co-administered with other QT-prolonging drugs. 3. Cyclosporine and pentamidine both increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. 4. Dasatinib and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Degarelix and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Desflurane and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Desipramine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Deutetrabenazine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent. However, certain conditions (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, congenital QT prolongation, or co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs) may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death. 9. Didanosine and pentamidine may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. There is an enhanced risk of pancreatitis. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 10. Disopyramide and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Dofetilide and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Dolasetron and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Donepezil and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Doxepin and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Dronedarone and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Droperidol and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Efavirenz and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Elagolix increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak CYP2C19 inhibitor, so caution is advised when used with sensitive CYP2C19 substrates. 19. Eliglustat and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Pentamidine and elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increase the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Encorafenib and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 22. Pentamidine and entecavir may increase each other's effects by decreasing renal clearance. Co-administration with drugs that reduce renal function or compete for active tubular secretion may increase serum concentrations of either entecavir or the co-administered drug. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Pentamidine and entrectinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Epinephrine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Racemic epinephrine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Eribulin and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If concurrent use is necessary, ECG monitoring is recommended. 27. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, or stearate) and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 29. Eslicarbazepine acetate increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Etravirine increases pentamidine levels by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely due to the potential for increased toxicity. 31. Ezogabine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with QT-prolonging agents. 32. Fedratinib increases the level or effect of pentamidine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of fedratinib (a CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 substrate) with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors. 33. Fexinidazole and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of fexinidazole with drugs known to block potassium channels and/or prolong the QT interval. 34. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of finerenone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 35. Fingolimod and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 36. Flecainide and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 37. Pentamidine increases the level or effect of flibanserin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Increased flibanserin adverse effects may occur if co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Fluconazole and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 39. Fluoxetine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 40. Fluphenazine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 41. Fluvoxamine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 42. Pentamidine decreases folic acid levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral form of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 43. Formoterol and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 44. Foscarnet and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Both drugs also increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor closely for severe hypocalcemia. 45. Pentamidine and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 46. Gadobenate and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Ganciclovir increases the toxicity of pentamidine through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 48. Gemifloxacin and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 49. Pentamidine and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Gentamicin and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 51. Gepirone and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Gilteritinib and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 53. Pentamidine and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs when initiating, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 54. Pentamidine and glasdegib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 55. Glucarpidase decreases the level or effect of pentamidine by increasing metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Leucovorin, reduced folates, and folate antimetabolites are substrates for glucarpidase, which hydrolyzes glutamate residues from folic acid and antifolates. 56. Goserelin increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. There is an increased risk of torsades de pointes. 57. Granisetron and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 58. Haloperidol and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 59. Histrelin increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. There is an increased risk of torsades de pointes. 60. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 61. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of pentamidine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. There is an increased risk of torsades de pointes. 62. Ibutilide and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 63. Ifosfamide and pentamidine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Renal function should be monitored. 64. Iloperidone and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 65. Imipramine and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 66. Indacaterol (inhaled) and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs known to prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 67. Indapamide and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 68. Inotuzumab and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use is unavoidable, obtain ECGs and electrolytes before and after initiation of any QTc-prolonging drug, and periodically monitor as clinically indicated during treatment. 69. Pentamidine and insulin (various formulations) may cause either hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, followed by the opposing effect. Use caution and monitor closely. Insulin dosage adjustment and increased glucose monitoring may be required.
